outcome: Incidence of intraoperative nausea and vomiting
Incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting
Severity of intraoperative nausea and vomiting
Severity of early postoperative nausea and vomiting
cohort: Pregnant women undergoing caesarean delivery with spinal anesthesia.
finding: Glycopyrrolate 0.2 mg iv was found to be more effective than dexamethasone, metoclopramide, and normal saline in preventing and controlling the incidence and severity of intraoperative and early postoperative nausea and vomiting after spinal anesthesia for caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Administration of glycopyrrolate intravenously before spinal anesthesia in caesarean section effectively controlled the incidence and severity of intraoperative and early postoperative nausea and vomiting compared to the non-treatment group.
